decisions.reason: It builds directly on the firm’s established recycling-system knowledge and has already shown strong customer value with reported savings of more than 600,000 euros per year, which the firm can further exploit through its R&D and service capabilities.

As a mobile slow-speed shredder close to the core offer, it fits the firm’s existing engineering, production and support knowledge base, and its continued dedicated presence suggests enough market traction to justify further learning and refinement rather than exit.

This modular waste-processing concept is highly related to the firm’s existing competences and has both quantified economic benefits and a named user reference, indicating that the firm can recognize, learn from and commercially scale the product.

Although newly launched in 2024, the product is very close to the firm’s established shredding activities, so absorptive capacity is high and management would typically allow more time to gather field feedback and improve the offer.

The mobile spiral shaft screens build on the firm’s established processing-system knowledge, and given the firm’s active R&D, university cooperation and industry growth, the prudent decision is to keep the product while assimilating early market and technical learning.
